title: 'Native module cannot be null' after eas update
symptom: App was fine; after an eas update, users crash on launch with 'Native module cannot be null'.
expected_root_cause: A binary release was smuggled out as an OTA — the OTA's JS imported a native module that isn't in the installed binary (the change touched package.json deps / an app.config plugin / ios|android), and either the runtimeVersion didn't change or version wasn't bumped
expected_fix: Restore the matching binary OR rebuild + bump runtimeVersion; prevent it with the fingerprint runtimeVersion policy (it hashes the native graph so EAS refuses to send native-needing JS to old binaries)
obvious_but_wrong: roll back JS / blame the new feature's React code
pebble_answer: Root cause: this is a binary release smuggled out as an OTA. The eas update shipped JS that imports a native module not present in the installed binary — the change actually touched package.json deps, an app.config.js plugin, or the ios/android native dirs, so it needed a new binary, not an OTA. EAS let the JS reach an old binary because the runtimeVersion did not change (or version was not bumped). Fix: restore the matching binary OR rebuild and bump the runtimeVersion. Prevent recurrence with the fingerprint runtimeVersion policy: it hashes the native dependency graph so EAS refuses to send native-needing JS to old binaries. Do NOT simply roll back the JS — that hides the boundary violation and it will recur on the next native-touching change.
source: Abiodun Abdullahi, 'The Realities of OTA Updates with Expo', 2026-04
